content.text: {"label":"marketing_campaign","explanation":"The general queue surge began right after the 11:30 fixed-deposit email to 750,000 customers, which asked them to 'call to book'. On general, volume was +37% at 12:00 and +45% at 12:15. new_offer_enquiry is running at 3.66x normal, and account_update is up 1.44x, possibly following on from the 08:45 KYC SMS. General staffing is close to plan (34 vs 35) and AHT is normal, so this is a demand problem caused by the campaign. Payments is a separate, smaller problem: volume and AHT are on forecast, but it is about 4 agents short (35 vs 39 planned, 4 sick against 2.8 usual), which pulled service level down to 25%. There is no open incident, so this is not an outage.","plan_name":"FD campaign surge response with payments staffing top-up","rationale":"Neither queue can lend agents because both are well below 70% service level, so cross-skilled moves are ruled out. For general, the plan cuts demand and adds capacity. Chat deflection takes FD offer enquiries cheaply. Callback flattens the peak while the email response is freshest. Delayed breaks and cancelled coaching free capacity during the next 1.5–2.5 hours. Two consecutive overtime offers cover the expected tail of the campaign until 17:00. For payments, overtime replaces part of the 4-agent absence gap, and chat deflection takes status and refund enquiries. Expected overtime cost is about Rs 10,000 at roughly 40% acceptance, within the Rs 15,000 budget. Chat cost should be roughly Rs
